{{Quote|No sound is more terrifying to the creatures of the Mandalorian night than the piercing cry of the ''jai'galaar'', the shriek-hawk. Shriek-hawks are peerless hunters, but never more dangerous than when defending their nests.|[[Tor Vizsla]]|<ref name="TBHC" />}}
'''Shriek-hawks''' were a [[Species/Legends|species]] of [[Bird/Legends|avian]] predator [[Homeworld/Legends|native]] to the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]] [[Planet/Legends|world]] of [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]]. Known as a '''''jai'galaar''''' in the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] [[Language/Legends|language]] of [[Mando'a/Legends|''Mando'a'']], the shriek-[[Hawk (animal)|hawk]] possessed a unique cry—loud and piercing—from which it earned its name. Its natural prowess as a hunter made the shriek-hawk an icon in the Mandalorian culture, inspiring traditional iconography such as the [[jaig eyes|''jaig'' eyes]] sigil, and the stylized symbol of [[Clan Vizsla/Legends|Clan Vizsla]].

==Biology and behavior==
Shriek-hawks were an [[Bird/Legends|avian]] [[Species/Legends|species]] [[Homeworld/Legends|indigenous]] to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]],<ref name="TBHC" /> located in the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim Territories]] of [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]].<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref> Efficient [[Hunting/Legends|predators]] who hunted their prey in the dark of night,<ref name="TBHC" /> shriek-hawks were winged and possessed sharp talons. They were known to strike from above, swooping and diving down upon their [[Death/Legends|kill]] with their wings folded back and their talons outstretched.<ref name="ImpCom501st">''[[Imperial Commando: 501st]]''</ref> Shriek-hawks had a unique, piercing cry, and were vigorous defenders of their nests.<ref name="TBHC" />

==History==
Native to the planet Mandalore, shriek-hawks evolved on the Outer Rim world and adapted to hunting<ref name="TBHC" /> in its varied environments.<ref name="TEA" /> The many creatures that called Mandalore their home came to fear the shriek-hawk's cry,<ref name="TBHC" /> and the [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorians]] took to calling the predatory avians ''jai'galaare''—a term in the [[Mando'a/Legends|''Mando'a'']] [[Language/Legends|language]] which meant "shriek-hawks," originating the name later used for the creature by [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]]-speaking society.<ref name="Mando'a">{{WebCite|url=http://www.karentraviss.com/page20/page26/index.html|text=Mando'a|author=Karen Traviss|work=[http://www.karentraviss.com Karen Traviss]|archivedate=20110925083955}}</ref>

[[File:DeathWatch-TMP.png|thumb|right|175px|The stylized sigil of [[Clan Vizsla/Legends|Clan Vizsla]], inspired by a diving shriek-hawk]]
The ''jai'galaar''{{'s}} reputation as a peerless hunter made the animal a well-known symbol in the Mandalorian culture. The Mandalorian [[Clan Vizsla/Legends|Vizsla clan]] took a stylized image<ref name="TCWCE">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''</ref> of a shriek-hawk in mid-dive<ref name="ImpCom501st" /> as the sigil of their clan.<ref name="TCWCE" /> Following the foundation of the radical [[Death Watch/Legends|Death Watch]] splinter group by [[Tor Vizsla]],<ref name="HotM">{{InsiderCite|80|The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors}}</ref> the shriek-hawk sigil of Clan Vizsla was adapted by the Death Watch.<ref name="TBHC" /> The shriek-hawk also inspired another Mandalorian sigil, [[Jaig eyes|''jai'galaar'la sur'haii'se'']], or "shriek-hawk [[Eye/Legends|eyes]]." These ''jaig'' eyes, as they were more commonly referred to, were a unique marking awarded by Mandalorian clan [[Chief/Legends|chieftains]] as a means of recognizing a [[Soldier/Legends|soldier's]] outstanding bravery.<ref name="TMPaC">{{InsiderCite|86|The Mandalorians: People and Culture}}</ref> The custom of awarding ''jaig'' eyes transferred to the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], whose Mandalorian training [[Sergeant/Legends|sergeants]] authorized distinguished [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] to wear the battlefield honor.<ref name="New Battlefronts" /> That same Mandalorian influence led the [[Clone Captain/Legends|clone captain]] and [[Clone trooper pilot/Legends|pilot]] [[Jai'galaar (clone)|CT-55/11-9009]] to take on the name Jai'galaar as his own,<ref name="GttGAR">{{InsiderCite|84|Guide to the Grand Army of the Republic}}</ref> in reference to the predatory bird.<ref name="TBHC" />

==Behind the scenes==
The term ''jai'galaar'' was introduced to ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[Star Wars Legends|Legends]] in the [[Star Wars Insider 84|eighty-fourth issue]] of ''[[Star Wars Insider]]'', where it was mentioned in reference to the clone trooper Captain Jai'galaar in [[Karen Traviss]] and [[Ryan Kaufman (real person)|Ryan Kaufman's]] article, the "[[Guide to the Grand Army of the Republic]]."<ref name="GttGAR" /> Traviss' subsequent article for the ''Insider'' magazine's [[Star Wars Insider 86|eighty-sixth]] issue, entitled "[[The Mandalorians: People and Culture]]," introduced the Basic translation of ''jai'galaar'' as shriek-hawk, and established the creature's connection to the Mandalorian homeworld and culture.<ref name="TMPaC" /> ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' mentioned the shriek-hawk under an informational entry on "''jai'galaar'',"<ref name="CSWE">''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]''</ref> and both the ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars Character Encyclopedia]]''<ref name="TCWCE" /> and [[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: New Battlefronts: The Visual Guide|''The Clone Wars: New Battlefronts: The Visual Guide'']] refer to the shriek-hawk in regard to the ''jaig'' eyes battle honors and Clan Vizsla's clan sigil.<ref name="New Battlefronts">''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars: New Battlefronts: The Visual Guide]]''</ref> Further information on shriek-hawks came with the release of ''[[The Bounty Hunter Code: From the Files of Boba Fett]]'' reference book in [[2013]].<ref name="TBHC" />
